comment: Senate Class II seats (last elected 2020), plus OH and FL special elections. dem_seats_not_up / rep_seats_not_up reflect current composition minus seats being contested.

races.note: Tommy Tuberville ran for governor, vacating the seat. R primary June 2026: Steve Marshall (AG) entered as frontrunner; Barry Moore and Jared Hudson also ran. D field is weak. Deep-red Alabama (R+27) is Safe R regardless of primary outcome.

Peltola challenging Sullivan with ranked-choice voting. 17 polls avg D+1.7. NYT/Siena (Jun '26): R+2.4 — pulling back from Alaska Survey Research peak of D+5 (Jun '26). Race has trended toward Peltola across the cycle (R+4 Aug '25 → D+2 Jan '26 → D+5 Jun '26) but the NYT/Siena result adds uncertainty. RCV and Peltola's crossover appeal keep this competitive. Toss-up.
Cotton seeking his third term in deep-red Arkansas. Democrat Hallie Shoffner, a farmer and first-time candidate, won the D primary. One poll (Cygnal Feb '26): Cotton R+22. Safe R.

Hickenlooper won his D primary (said to be his final Senate term). R field has not produced a top-tier recruit; Colorado has shifted solidly blue at the federal level. No general election polling. Safe D.
Coons running for a fourth term in deep-blue Delaware. R primary produced only minor candidates. No Republican has won a Delaware Senate race since 1994. Safe D.

Vacancy election for Rubio's seat. Moody (R, appointed) vs Vindman (D, likely nominee; D primary Aug 26). 15 polls avg R+6.8. UNF (Jul '26): Vindman R+9.7, Nixon R+8.4 — most recent. Change Research (Jun '26, LV): Even — remains the most D-favorable outlier. Moody consistently ahead in most polls. Likely R.

Ossoff (D incumbent, won 2021 runoff by 1.2 pts) vs Mike Collins (R, won May 19 primary). 23 polls avg D+6.5. Most recent: Fabrizio Ward/AARP (Jul '26): D+9; Wick (Jun '26): D+3.8; Beacon Research (Jun '26, rv): D+13. Ossoff has led in every poll. Key D hold.

Risch (age 83) running for re-election with Trump's endorsement. David Roth is the D nominee. First polling: Bullfinch Group (Jun '26): Roth R+17 vs Risch (rv). Deep-red Idaho (R+32) keeps this Safe R.

Dick Durbin retired after 48 years. Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton won the D primary (March 17) with 40% over Krishnamoorthi and Kelly. Former IL GOP chair Don Tracy won the R primary. Stratton is heavily favored in deep-blue Illinois (D+17 PVI). Safe D.

Ernst retired; Hinson (R) vs Turek (D), both won June 3 primaries. 10 polls avg R+1.0. Most recent: Beacon Research (Jun '26, rv): D+4; NYT/Siena (Jun '26): R+2.5 — highest-quality poll shows Hinson ahead. Very competitive; within 3 pts across all recent polling.

Marshall seeking re-election with minimal R primary opposition. D primary Aug 4: Patrick Schmidt is the leading D candidate. Two polls avg R+6: Tavern Research (Jan '26) R+8 vs generic D; GQR (Apr '26, D-sponsored): Schmidt R+4. Deep-red Kansas (R+20) is Safe R regardless of D nominee.

McConnell retired after 42 years. R primary: Rep. Andy Barr, former AG Daniel Cameron, Nate Morris. D candidate: Charles Booker. Dec '25 PPP polls (D-sponsored) show: Morris R+1 vs Booker — surprisingly close; Cameron R+7; Barr R+11. Avg across named R matchups: R+6.3. R+26 PVI keeps this Safe R regardless of R nominee.

Louisiana uses a jungle primary: all candidates appear on the November ballot together. If no one clears 50%, top two advance to a December runoff. Cassidy faces Rep. Julia Letlow (Trump-endorsed, running due to Cassidy's vote to convict Trump) and former Rep. John Fleming on the R side. D field is weak. Safe R.

Troy Jackson (Maine Senate President) is the D nominee after Graham Platner withdrew in late July following a rape allegation and pressure from national Democratic leaders, who pulled key endorsements. Jackson was selected by the party over the weekend of July 25-26. Jackson polls significantly stronger than Platner, who had trailed Collins R+3 to R+5 in July polling. Jackson-specific polls (3): Wedgewood D+5, PPP D+5 (D-spon), UNH D+3 — avg D+4.3. Overall 34-poll average (including Platner history): D+1.2. Collins (30-year incumbent) remains a strong candidate, but Jackson represents a materially better matchup for Democrats. Genuine toss-up.

Markey (incumbent D) vs Moulton (D primary challenger, Aug 4) vs Deaton (R). UNH (Jun '26): Moulton D+20, Markey D+16 — Moulton now outpolls Markey by 4 pts vs Deaton. 8 polls avg D+25.4. Baker (former Gov.) entered the R primary; no Baker vs D matchups yet. Safe D regardless of D or R nominee.

Peters retiring. D primary Aug 4: McMorrow, Stevens, El-Sayed vs Mike Rogers (R). 39 polls avg R+1.0. Most recent (Jun '26): Wedgewood: Stevens Even, El-Sayed D+5, McMorrow R+7; Quantus: Stevens D+1.4, El-Sayed D+1.1, McMorrow R+0.9; Data for Progress: Stevens R+1, El-Sayed D+1. El-Sayed improving; Stevens vs Rogers still the closest matchup overall. Primary outcome will determine competitiveness.

Smith retiring. D primary Aug 4: Flanagan vs Craig vs Tafoya (R). Impact Research (May '26, D-spon): both Flanagan and Craig D+7. 10 polls avg D+5.0. Mason-Dixon (Jun '26): generic D+8. Likely D hold.

Hyde-Smith won the R primary (March 10) with 81%. She faces Democrat Scott Colom, Lowndes County DA. One poll (Impact Research Apr '26, D-sponsored): Colom R+3. No Democrat has won a MS Senate race since 1982. Safe R.

Daines withdrew; Alme (R) vs Bankhead (D). 5 polls avg R+15.0. Hart Research (Jun '26, D-spon): R+6 head-to-head — significant D-favorable outlier; Public Opinion Strategies (Jun '26, R-spon): R+19; Tavern Research (May '26): generic D R+12. Montana remains solidly R.

Dan Osborn (Independent) challenging Ricketts, appointed in 2023 after Sasse resigned. Osborn nearly beat Fischer in 2024. Two Osborn-specific polls: Impact Research (Feb '26): R+1; Change Research (Mar '25): R+1. Avg R+1.0. Note: NE R+22 PVI heavily offsets this in the fundamentals blend. Osborn's Independent appeal may outperform model — modeled on D side.

Shaheen retiring. Pappas (D) vs Sununu (R) confirmed matchup; Brown also in R primary (Sept). Pappas vs Sununu: 12 polls avg D+3.5 (range D+1 to D+7). Most recent: St. Anselm (Jun '26): D+6; UNH (Jun '26): D+3; Peak Insights (Jun '26, R-spon): D+1. Pappas vs Brown: avg D+12. Overall avg (all matchups): D+6.7. If Sununu wins R primary, competitive battleground. Lean D.
Booker seeking a third full term in deep-blue New Jersey. R primary produced no top-tier recruit. NJ has not elected a Republican senator since 1972. Safe D.

Only GOP candidate (Christopher Vanden Heuvel) disqualified for insufficient petition signatures — the first time in modern NM history with no Republican on the Senate ballot. Luján runs effectively unopposed. Safe D.

Open seat; Cooper (D, former governor) vs Whatley (R). 23 polls avg D+7.3. Most recent: PPP (Jul '26, D-spon): D+4; NYT/Siena (Jun '26): D+6.8; YouGov/Catawba (Jun '26): D+13.7. Cooper leads in every poll. Top D pickup opportunity. Likely D.

Mullin confirmed as DHS Secretary, resigned March 23; Gov. Stitt appointed Alan Armstrong. Armstrong pledged not to run for the full term. R primary June 16: Rep. Kevin Hern was the frontrunner. D primary: Evan Beck, Jim Priest among declared candidates. Deep-red Oklahoma (R+26) remains Safe R.
Merkley seeking a fourth term. Oregon has not elected a Republican senator since 2002. Safe D.
Reed seeking a sixth term vs Raymond McKay (R). First poll: UNH (Jun '26): D+17. RI has not elected a Republican senator since 2000. Safe D.

Lindsey Graham died July 11, 2026. His sister was appointed to hold the seat through the election but is not running. Race is now fully open with no incumbent on the ballot. R primary will determine who faces Annie Andrews. PPP (Jul '26, D-spon) tests 5 R candidates vs Andrews: Norman R+1, Sanford D+1, Lynch D+3, Fry D+3, Mace D+3. Andrews runs competitive vs all tested R candidates (non-Graham avg D+1.8). R+11 PVI still makes this Safe R, but the open seat and Andrews' strength merit watching.

rep.name: TBD (R primary: Norman / Fry / Mace / others)

races.note: Rounds seeking a third term. D candidate: Julian Beaudion. 3 polls avg R+21.3: PPP (Nov '25) R+22, PPP (Feb '26) R+17, PPP (May '26) R+25. Deep-red South Dakota (R+27) — Safe R.
Hagerty seeking a second term with Trump's endorsement. No R primary challenger; D field has not produced a serious candidate. Deep-red Tennessee (R+26) — Safe R.

Cornyn retired; Paxton (R, won runoff May 24) vs Talarico (D). Open seat. 24 polls avg R+0.9. Most recent: NYT/Siena (Jun '26): R+0.1 — essentially tied; A2 Insights (Jun '26): D+2.3. Race remains a genuine toss-up despite R+10 PVI. Bruising Cornyn-Paxton primary may be helping Talarico.

Warner seeking a fourth term. Leading R challenger Bryce Reeves (state Sen.) withdrew Dec 2025; no top-tier R recruit has emerged. No general election polling. Virginia has trended D at the federal level; Warner's strong brand keeps this Likely D.
Capito seeking a third term with Trump's endorsement. R primary challenge from convicted Jan. 6 participant Derrick Evans poses no real threat. Deep-red West Virginia (R+30) — Safe R.
Lummis announced in December 2025 she will not seek re-election. Rep. Harriet Hageman, endorsed by Lummis, is the R primary frontrunner (Aug 18). Deep-red Wyoming (R+35) — Safe R.

Vacancy election for Vance's seat. Brown (D) vs Husted (R). 15 polls avg R+0.6. Trend is volatile: June showed Brown leading (D+3 to D+8), but NYT/Siena (Jun 28 '26): R+2.8 — highest-quality poll pulls average back to R. Race has been: Husted +6 early '25 → near-even Apr '26 → Brown leading Jun '26 → Husted R+2.8. Genuine toss-up; watch for sustained trend.
